critique_of_multiway_peer: Multiway specialist is the most rigorous of the three R1 panel takes and the load-bearing arguments are clean: (1) MP's 26% sizing is range-merged not polar (overpairs + Qx + sets + straights + 77-88 floaters + AhX backdoor) so fold equity from a hero raise is structurally small; (2) CO's flat-then-call chain is range-capped but densely concentrated in QJ9-smashing combos (JJ-some, 99, QJs, JTs, T9s, KTs, KQs, J9s) that won't fold to flop pressure; (3) AdKd is the textbook bluff-raise candidate that gets blown off equity when 3-bet by CO's slowplayed straight/set. Their ~mid-30s raw equity estimate is well-calibrated and avoids the equity-overcounting trap Opus falls into. Their 80/20 mix is reasonable; my 88/12 trims further because AdKd specifically (vs the KTs/T9s/JTs-blocker combos they correctly identify as the raise slice) is NOT in that combo group, so the raise frequency on this exact hand-class skews lower than the cluster average.
critique_of_range_construction_peer: Range-construction correctly identifies the range-architecture tension — hero NEEDS bluff-raise candidates in this node to balance KT/AT/sets/two-pair value raises, and the A-blocker/K-blocker logic genuinely removes nut-straight combos from villain ranges. The 70/30 mix and MEDIUM confidence are defensible from pure structural-balance theory. However, their argument under-weights the load-bearing CO-sandwich constraint that the multiway peer surfaces: even if AKo is structurally a defensible raise-bluff candidate by blocker logic, the CO-still-live cap-then-uncapped-strong dynamic makes the raise EV-negative in execution because CO continues sticky and MP doesn't fold his merged range. I would trim their RAISE slice from 30% to ~12-15% on the same combo, with the residual raise frequency surviving for range-construction balance reasons rather than EV-positive execution.
critique_of_sonnet_split: Sonnet 3 CALL / 2 RAISE. The 3 CALL voters (1, 2, 3) all converge on the correct GTO load-bearing arguments: pot odds ~21% vs ~30-35% raw equity, nut-gutshot implied odds on T turns, IP-closing realization ~0.85, and the structural problem that raising folds out air we crush and gets called only by hands that crush us. These are textbook GTO arguments and they're correctly applied. The 2 RAISE voters (4, 5) make a credible-sounding semi-bluff case (10+ outs, charge draws, fold equity vs MP air, build pot for nut hits) but commit two errors the panel correctly identifies: (a) labeller 4 misreads the bet size as ~36% pot when it's ~26% — at 26% the price-to-peel is so cheap that fold equity has to do much more work to justify raising; (b) both RAISE voters under-weight the CO-sandwich constraint, treating the spot as if CO will fold to the raise when CO's continuing range on QJ9 is dense in straights/sets/two-pair/big-draws that won't fold and can re-raise. The Sonnet majority is correct.
critique_of_opus_tierup: Opus's value/protection argument is structurally familiar — IP-closing semi-bluff on wet board with nut redraw — but the execution misses two load-bearing GTO checks. First, Opus claims 'raw equity vs MP's c-bet range ~48-52%' which is wildly optimistic; against MP's actual 26%-sizing range (which retains overpairs, sets, Qx, two-pair, KT/T8s straights) AdKd is closer to ~30-35% raw, not 48-52%. The equity inflation drives the entire raise-EV argument. Second, Opus dismisses the CO-sandwich with the assertion that the raise 'folds CO's capped continuance' — but earlier in the same reasoning Opus describes CO's range as 'sticky range that won't fold to a flop raise' (QJs/JTs/KJs/QTs/KQs/T9s/T8s/JJ-set/suited connectors). Opus's own range-construction contradicts the fold-equity claim. The MEDIUM confidence flag is appropriate but Opus still lands on the wrong modal action. From a GTO lens: Opus correctly identifies that AdKd is mixable RAISE/CALL, but inverts the mix — RAISE is the minority (~12-15%) not the modal action. The CO-sandwich constraint is the binding GTO driver that Opus's value/protection frame under-weights.
revised_reasoning: Standing by CALL HIGH at 87/13 mix, essentially unchanged from R1 (88/12). The panel unanimous CALL converges on the same GTO-load-bearing argument I made in R1, and Round 2 exposure to the Sonnet RAISE voters and Opus tier-up does not move the verdict. What I stand by: (1) Pot odds 2.5 into 12 = 20.8% required, hero clears comfortably on nut-gutshot + BDFD + overcard equity even with multiway haircuts; (2) MP's 26% range-bet is merged not polar, so fold equity from a raise is structurally small; (3) CO's call-call chain caps range but concentrates density in QJ9-smashing combos (JJ-some/99/QJs/JTs/T9s/KTs/KQs) that won't fold to a flop raise and can re-raise with the strong tail; (4) AKo's blocker profile is genuinely poor for a raise — blocks AQ/AJ (folding anyway) and blocks KQ/AK-other (calling anyway), while NOT blocking the JJ/99/QJ/JT/T9 cluster that crushes us; (5) IP-closing realization is high (~0.90), preserving the gutshot equity-realization at a discount. What Round 2 updated: my critique of Opus sharpens — Opus's 48-52% equity claim is the load-bearing error driving the RAISE verdict, and Opus's own CO range description ('sticky, won't fold') internally contradicts the fold-equity argument. The 2 Sonnet RAISE voters make the semi-bluff case more credibly than Opus (no equity-inflation), but still under-weight the CO-sandwich. Range-Construction's structural balance argument is theoretically valid but execution-EV-negative — AdKd specifically is in the bluff-raise combo group only at low frequency because the better raise candidates (KTs/T9s/JTs/QTss-blocker) carry made-equity + redraws that AKo lacks. Final GTO call: CALL is the modal pure strategy at ~87% frequency, RAISE survives at ~13% for range-balance against value raises (KT/AT/sets), FOLD remains dominated by price + equity + position + nut-blocker profile. Verdict: CALL HIGH.
